title: WHO ICD-11 Reference Guide - Chapter 26: Traditional Medicine Module 2
text: Traditional Medicine Module 2 (TM2) enables standardized recording of Ayurveda, Siddha, and Unani morbidity patterns. Diagnostic patterns such as Jwara (pyrexial disorders) map to specific febrile disorder categories in ICD-11 biomedicine and TM2 pattern designations.

title: National AYUSH Morbidity and Standardized Terminologies Electronic (NAMASTE) Portal
source: Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India
text: National Ayurveda Morbidity Codes (NAMC) define diagnostic conditions, dosha derangements, and clinical manifestations based on classical Ayurvedic compendia (Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita).

title: Charaka Samhita - Chikitsa Sthana (Chapter 3: Jwara Chikitsitam)
text: Jwara is the lord of all diseases characterized by Santapa (elevated heat/temperature), Aruchi (anorexia), Trishna (excessive thirst), Angamarda (body ache), and Hridvyatha (restlessness).

title: ICD-11 Entity Specification: MG26 Symptoms or signs involving the body temperature
text: MG26 covers pyrexia of unknown origin, hyperpyrexia, and elevated body temperature in response to systemic inflammation, infection, or thermoregulatory disturbance.

title: ICD-11 Entity Specification: MD30 Cough
text: MD30 describes cough as a sudden, repetitive reflex response to airway irritation or respiratory conditions, corresponding closely with Ayurvedic Kasa roga.
